extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners, third-party requesters, and practitioners handling inter partes reexamination appeals (U.S. USPTO)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules in the MPEP governing examiner answers, rebuttal briefs, oral hearings, Board decisions (including new grounds of rejection), rehearing, remands, and issuance of Notices of Intent to Issue Inter Partes Reexamination Certificates in inter partes reexamination appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's answer must explain disagreements and identify affected claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s answer must include an explanation of the reasons for disagreement with any such contentions. If any ground of rejection or inapplicability of proposed rejection is not argued and responded to by the appropriate party, the examiner must point out each claim affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each contention is addressed and explicitly identify every claim affected when a ground is not argued/responded to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Proceedings Appendix requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of any decisions rendered by a court or the Board in any proceeding identified by the examiner in the Related Appeals and Interferences section of the answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach copies of judicial or Board decisions referenced in Related Proceedings to the answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and signature/initialing of examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner’s answer is complete, the examiner will sign it. On the examiner’s answer, each conferee who was present at the appeal conference will place his/her initials below the signature of the examiner who prepared the answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type conferee name as 'John Smith (conferee)' and initial as e.g., 'JS'. Initialing by conferee does not necessarily indicate concurrence with the answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing and forms with examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: The CRU technical support staff will mail a copy of the examiner’s answer to the patent owner and to the third party requester(s). The technical support staff should attach form PTOL-2070 to the copy of the answer to be mailed to the third party requester by the CRU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure correct attachments (PTOL-2070) and mailing to all parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to CRU Director for novel legal interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner’s answer is believed to contain a new interpretation or application of the existing patent law, the examiner’s answer, the case file, and an explanatory memorandum should be forwarded to the CRU Director for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forward matters raising new legal interpretations to CRU Director per MPEP §1003.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal brief filing deadline (one month)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any appellant may file a rebuttal brief under § 41.71 within one month of the date of the examiner’s answer. The time for filing a rebuttal brief or an amended rebuttal brief may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict one-month, non-extendable deadline from mailing date of examiner’s answer to file a rebuttal brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner's rebuttal brief scope and prohibition on new evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The rebuttal brief of the owner may be directed to the examiner’s answer and/or any respondent brief. The rebuttal brief of the owner shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or an affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit owner rebuttal to responses to answer/respondent briefs; do not introduce new/amended claims or new affidavits/evidence (see 37 CFR 1.116 and 41.63 for exceptions/timing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester rebuttal brief limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The rebuttal brief of any requester may be directed to the examiner’s answer and/or the respondent brief of the owner. The rebuttal brief of a requester may not be directed to the respondent brief of any other requester. No new ground of rejection can be proposed by a requester. The rebuttal brief of a requester shall not include any new or non-admitted affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters may only respond to examiner’s answer and owner respondent brief; cannot propose new rejections or include new evidence or address other requesters’ briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of service required for rebuttal briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: The rebuttal brief must include a certification that a copy of the rebuttal brief has been served in its entirety on all other parties to the proceeding. The names and addresses of the parties served must be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear service certificate naming and giving addresses of all parties served.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cure period for noncompliant but timely rebuttal briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rebuttal brief is timely filed but does not comply with all the requirements, appellant will be notified of the reasons for non-compliance and provided with a non-extendable period of one month within which to file an amended rebuttal brief. If the appellant does not file an amended rebuttal brief during the one-month period, or files an amended rebuttal brief which does not overcome all the reasons for non-compliance, that appellant’s rebuttal brief and any amended rebuttal brief by that appellant will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One non-extendable one-month cure opportunity; failure to cure means the brief is not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal brief must identify issues and point to where raised
rubrics_metrics.description: The rebuttal brief must (A) clearly identify each issue, and (B) point out where the issue was raised in the examiner’s answer and/or in the respondent brief. In addition, the rebuttal brief must be limited to issues raised in the examiner’s answer or in any respondent brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each issue in the rebuttal must be specifically identified and traced to where it was originally raised; briefs not so limited will not be entered or considered (they will remain in file but not addressed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Only rebuttal briefs accepted after examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: After the examiner’s answer, only a rebuttal brief (or an amended rebuttal brief where appellant is given one opportunity to correct a defective original rebuttal brief) will be received into the reexamination proceeding. No other submission will be considered, and any such other submission will be returned as an improper paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit other papers after the examiner’s answer; they will be returned under 37 CFR 1.939.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when no rebuttal brief is filed
rubrics_metrics.description: If no rebuttal brief is received within the one month period set in the examiner’s answer, the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) will issue a notification letter to parties using form paragraph 26.67, and will then forward the reexamination proceeding to the Board for decision on the appeal(s). Prosecution remains closed. Any further reply/comments by any party will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRU will notify and forward to Board; prosecution closed; further submissions not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board review and forwarding of rebuttal briefs to examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: When a rebuttal brief is received in response to an examiner’s answer, it is reviewed by the Board and then forwarded to the CRU for the examiner to consider the submission(s) and acknowledge the rebuttal brief using a Form PTOL-90.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board initially reviews rebuttal briefs; examiner acknowledgment via PTOL-90; examples of acknowledgement wording are provided in MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening prosecution to address a rebuttal brief requires CRU Director approval
rubrics_metrics.description: In a very rare situation, where the examiner finds that it is essential to address a rebuttal brief, the examiner must reopen prosecution. In order to reopen prosecution after an examiner’s answer, the CRU Director must approve the same in writing, at the end of the action that reopens prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reopening after answer is exceptional and requires written CRU Director approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing request timing, caption, fee and service certification
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appellant or a respondent desires an oral hearing, he or she must file, as a separate paper captioned 'REQUEST FOR ORAL HEARING,' a written request for such hearing accompanied by the fee set forth in § 41.20(b)(3) within two months after the date of the examiner’s answer. The time for requesting an oral hearing may not be extended. The request must include a certification that a copy of the request has been served in its entirety on all other parties to the proceeding. The names and addresses of the parties served must be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File a separately captioned request with fee within two months of examiner’s answer and include service certificate; no extensions allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: If no timely oral hearing request/fee, appeal decided on briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: If no request and fee for oral hearing have been timely filed by appellant or respondent as required, the appeal will be assigned for consideration and decision on the briefs without an oral hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing of request+fee is prerequisite to oral hearing participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing participation and scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant or respondent has complied with all requirements, a hearing date will be set and notice given to the owner and all requesters. The notice shall set a non-extendable period within which all requests for oral hearing shall be submitted by any other party to the appeal desiring to participate in the oral hearing. The Board will determine the order of the arguments presented at the oral hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board issues notice with non-extendable participation period; Board controls argument order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for oral argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral argument will be limited to thirty minutes for each appellant or respondent who has requested an oral hearing, and twenty minutes for the primary examiner unless otherwise ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare arguments to fit within strict time allocations; exceptions only by order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and argument limitations at oral hearing; new arguments on good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: At the oral hearing, each appellant and respondent may only rely on evidence that has been previously entered and considered by the primary examiner and present argument that has been relied upon in the briefs except as permitted by paragraph (e)(2). Upon a showing of good cause, appellant, respondent and/or the primary examiner may rely on a new argument based upon a recent relevant decision of either the Board or a Federal Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit presentations to previously entered record; new arguments allowed only for recent controlling decisions upon showing good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to oral hearings and procedure to close hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral hearings are open to the public as observers unless one of the appellants and/or the respondents (A) petitions under 37 CFR 41.3 that the hearing not be open to the public, (B) presents sufficient reasons, (C) pays the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 41.20(a), and (D) the petition is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To close hearing to public, file petition under 41.3 with reasons and fee; Board must grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decision authority and new grounds of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Trial and Appeal Board, in its decision, may affirm or reverse each decision of the examiner on all issues raised on each appealed claim, or remand the reexamination proceeding to the examiner for further consideration. The reversal of the examiner’s determination not to make a rejection proposed by the third party requester constitutes a decision adverse to the patentability of the claims ... which will be set forth in the decision of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board as a new ground of rejection under paragraph (b) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may enter new grounds; reversals of examiner’s refusals to adopt requester rejections become new grounds adverse to patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner options after Board new ground of rejection and one-month deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board makes a new ground of rejection, the owner, within one month from the date of the decision, must exercise one of the following two options to avoid termination of the appeal proceeding as to the rejected claim: (1) Reopen prosecution by filing an amendment and/or new evidence; or (2) Request rehearing by the Board under § 41.79, stating with particularity the points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner has one non-extendable month to choose between reopening (extensions under 1.956 available) or requesting rehearing (no extensions). Responses must be timely and sufficiently particular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester comments following owner response to new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the owner has filed a response requesting reopening of prosecution under paragraph (b)(1), any requester, within one month of the date of service of the owner’s response, may once file comments on the response. Such written comments must be limited to the issues raised by the Board’s opinion reflecting its decision and the owner’s response. Any requester that had not previously filed an appeal or cross appeal and is seeking under this subsection to file comments or a reply is subject to the appeal and brief fees under § 41.20(b)(1) and (2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters have a one-month window to comment limited to Board issues; fees apply if they previously had not appealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand handling after owner response and comment windows
rubrics_metrics.description: Following any response by the owner under paragraph (b)(1) and any written comments from a requester under paragraph (c), the proceeding will be remanded to the examiner. The examiner will consider any owner response and any written comments and issue a determination that the rejection is maintained or has been overcome. Within one month of the examiner’s determination, owner or any requester may once submit comments in response; within one month of service of comments, owner and any requesters may file a reply to the comments. No requester reply may address comments of any other requester reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict one-month windows for post-remand comments and replies; remand limited to consideration of new submission(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing request requirements and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for rehearing must state with particularity the points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked in rendering the Board’s opinion. Arguments not raised in the briefs before the Board and evidence not previously relied upon in the briefs are not permitted in the request for rehearing except as permitted by paragraphs (b)(2) and (b)(3): upon a showing of good cause, a party may present a new argument based upon a recent relevant decision of the Board or a Federal Court, and new arguments responding to a new ground of rejection are permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehearing limited to matters on the record except narrowly for recent controlling decisions or responses to new grounds; must be filed within one month; opposing parties may file comments in opposition within one month; time periods not extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on rehearing and finality for judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party files a request for rehearing, the Board shall render a decision on the request for rehearing. The decision on the request for rehearing is deemed to incorporate the earlier opinion reflecting its decision for appeal, except for those portions specifically withdrawn on rehearing and is final for the purpose of judicial review, except when noted otherwise in the decision on rehearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board’s rehearing decision typically becomes the final decision for judicial review; if rehearing generates a new decision, further rehearing may be sought within one month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action following Board decision and appeal to Federal Circuit
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties to an appeal to the Board may not appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit until all parties’ rights to request rehearing have been exhausted, at which time the decision of the Board is final and appealable by any party to the appeal to the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not file Federal Circuit appeal until rehearing rights are exhausted; two-month appellate timing rules apply once final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening after final Board decision requires Director authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: When a decision by the Patent Trial and Appeal Board on appeal has become final for judicial review, prosecution of the inter partes reexamination proceeding will not be reopened or reconsidered by the primary examiner except under the provisions of § 41.77 ... without the written authority of the Director, and then only for the consideration of matters not already adjudicated, sufficient cause being shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-final reopening is exceptional and requires Director written authority and sufficient cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIRC issuance when no new grounds and no party action
rubrics_metrics.description: If no action has been taken by any party to the appeal and at least two weeks after the time for action has expired, the CRU support staff will notify the examiner that the proceeding is ready to be concluded. The examiner will take up the reexamination proceeding for action by issuing a Notice of Intent to Issue Inter Partes Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) in accordance with MPEP § 2687, which will terminate the prosecution of the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIRC indicates status of all claims as result of Board decision and includes statements cancelling claims as appropriate; special handling guidance exists for dependent claims (e.g., converting dependent claims to independent form or cancelling) with specified time periods and extension rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board new-ground decisions are non-final and limit immediate court appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision which includes a new ground of rejection or a remand will be considered a non-final decision. Until the Board issues a final decision, the parties to the appeal to the Board may not appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit under 37 CFR 41.81.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New-ground or remand decisions do not permit immediate appeal; owner must take required follow-on steps permitted by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on filing both rehearing and reopening for same decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Board applies new ground(s) of rejection to at least one claim, the patent owner may file either a response requesting a reopening of prosecution relating to the new ground(s) of rejection or a request for rehearing under 37 CFR 41.79(a)(2) of the new ground(s) of rejection based on the same record. In other words, patent owner may not file both a response requesting a reopening of prosecution and also a request for rehearing under 37 CFR 41.79(a) for the same decision. A patent owner may also not file both a request for rehearing and a conditional request to reopen in the event that the request for rehearing is denied. If such an improper conditional request to reopen prosecution is received, then the submission will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution under 37 CFR 41.77(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit conflicting/conditional filings; conditional reopenings are treated as reopenings and may have adverse procedural consequences (e.g., termination of appeal to newly rejected claims).
